# Task-guidance test cases

These six cases cover bounded task handoff, full-stack decomposition, valid
component ownership, and compatibility-preserving migration. Each case uses a
fixed compact project and a reviewed target that is not included in the user
prompt.

## Scenario TG-01 — Eleventy archive pagination as one task

**Project:** a public static blog generated by Eleventy.

**User task:** keep `/blog/` as the first archive page, add stable later pages
with at most twenty posts, and add accessible previous/next navigation without
changing home, tags, feed, sitemap, post navigation, order, or zero-JavaScript
output.

**What it tests:** a cohesive cross-template feature should remain one task.
Retained-plan and omitted-plan handoffs should preserve public URL questions,
protected generated surfaces, and real production-build evidence.

**Expected shape:** one task file.

**Important connection:** real Eleventy configuration and templates must
produce the expected public files.

[Detailed evaluator contract](../../../agent-evaluation/suites/task_guidance/scenarios/01-eleventy-archive-single-task.md)

## Scenario TG-02 — FastAPI notes pagination as one task

**Project:** a public REST API backed by SQLite through FastAPI and an async
database adapter.

**User task:** add optional limit/offset pagination and a total-count response
header while preserving unparameterized list behavior, normal FastAPI
validation, and all other CRUD routes.

**What it tests:** one bounded public endpoint capability should remain one
task. The handoff must preserve unresolved public behavior without turning SQL,
ORM calls, tests, or documentation work into product requirements.

**Expected shape:** one task file.

**Important connection:** the production HTTP route must exercise the real
storage behavior that controls ordering, slicing, and total count.

[Detailed evaluator contract](../../../agent-evaluation/suites/task_guidance/scenarios/02-fastapi-pagination-single-task.md)

## Scenario TG-03 — Flask/Vue selected-filter refresh regression

**Project:** a user-facing Flask/Vue CRUD application.

**User task:** preserve the selected All/Read/Unread filter after add, edit,
and delete refreshes while keeping active-state visibility, API response shape,
and unfiltered behavior.

**What it tests:** a bounded full-stack regression should remain one cohesive
task. Add/update/delete are variants of one outcome, not separate requirements
or subtasks.

**Expected shape:** one task file.

**Important connection:** Vue state and refresh behavior must use the
production client transport, reach the Flask route, and render the returned
filtered result.

[Detailed evaluator contract](../../../agent-evaluation/suites/task_guidance/scenarios/03-flask-vue-filter-refresh-single-task.md)

## Scenario TG-04 — Flask/Vue book-discovery decomposition

**Project:** a larger full-stack books application with no existing filter,
search, pagination, or URL-state capability.

**User task:** add read-status filtering, title/author search, bounded
pagination, and shareable/restorable URL state while preserving CRUD and
unparameterized compatibility.

**What it tests:** agents should not create separate server, client, test, and
documentation phases. Each child should deliver a usable product capability
through the full stack.

**Expected shape:** approximately four vertical capabilities; three to five
children are acceptable when each has independent product value.

**Important connection:** every capability crosses Vue state and rendering,
the production client transport, Flask routing, and data selection.

[Detailed evaluator contract](../../../agent-evaluation/suites/task_guidance/scenarios/04-flask-vue-book-discovery-release.md)

## Scenario TG-05 — FastAPI service, client, and CLI query capability

**Project:** a public FastAPI service, an independently maintained Python
client package, and a CLI that consumes the client.

**User task:** define and deliver bounded pagination, stable sorting, and
optional text filtering across all three consumers while preserving existing
unparameterized behavior.

**What it tests:** component boundaries are valid when they have independent
ownership, compatibility, users, and acceptance. Each component should still
keep its implementation, focused tests, and documentation together.

**Expected shape:** shared contract, service, client, and CLI/integration
deliverables.

**Important connections:** HTTP route to storage, client transport to service,
and CLI through the real client package and HTTP service.

[Detailed evaluator contract](../../../agent-evaluation/suites/task_guidance/scenarios/05-fastapi-multi-consumer-query-capability.md)

## Scenario TG-06 — Eleventy author-metadata compatibility migration

**Project:** a static site with legacy author front matter, generated pages,
archives, feeds, and a repository-owned authoring helper.

**User task:** migrate to structured multi-author metadata without breaking
existing content or output, and reject the legacy form only after direct
evidence shows nothing depends on it.

**What it tests:** migration work should be divided by safe working states,
not by parser, template, feed, content, helper, test, documentation, and
cleanup phases.

**Expected shape:** compatibility introduction, generated-surface adoption,
content/tool migration, and evidence-gated legacy retirement. Three to five
children are acceptable when every intermediate revision remains publishable.

**Important connection:** real front matter must pass through normalization
and the production Eleventy build into pages, archives, and feeds at each
migration state.

[Detailed evaluator contract](../../../agent-evaluation/suites/task_guidance/scenarios/06-eleventy-author-metadata-migration.md)
